author: Today I Found Out
description:
At 5:57 AM on July 21, 2011, a unique era of manned spaceflight came to an end as the Space Shuttle Atlantis touched down on Earth for the last time. The world’s first - and thus far only - operational spaceplane, over its 30 year career the Shuttle flew 135 missions carrying 355 astronauts from 16 different countries - almost 70% of all the people who have ever travelled into space. Designed as a reusable and reliable “space truck” that took off like a rocket, landed like a plane, and could be quickly refurbished between flights, the Shuttle promised to usher in an era of routine, cost effective, and safe orbital spaceflight. 

But while the Shuttle certainly did stellar service to mankind, becoming the iconic face of NASA post-Apollo, the technical and economic reality of the Shuttle program did not live up to its designers’ expectations.
